A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable text, equations, tables and figures. V1 ends after its references; v2 adds Appendix A. Content can be matched across the UL3D-to-UA3D rename, table consolidation and figure redesigns.

before.justification: V1 reports original detection experiments on nuScenes and Lyft, uncertainty ablations in Tables 3–4, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original detection experiments and reports additional granularity, auxiliary-loss-weight and attachment-layer ablations in Table 2b and Appendix A.5.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure remains auxiliary-versus-primary dense prediction disagreement, coordinate-level uncertainty regularization and primary-only inference. V2 expands the equations and architecture description and clarifies pseudo-box supervision; these changes do not establish a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate unsupervised object discovery on nuScenes and Lyft, including the same distance ranges. Additional qualitative examples retain the existing distant/small-object scenarios; no new dataset, domain or task is evaluated.

E2.justification: V2 adds box-level and point-cloud-level uncertainty alternatives as evaluated comparators to coordinate-level regularization in Table 2b. The existing supervised, MODEST-PP, MODEST, OYSTER and rule-based comparator memberships remain unchanged in their corresponding comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 adds controlled settings for uncertainty aggregation, auxiliary-loss weights of 0.25/0.5/1/2, and attachment at sa_layer_4/fp_layer_1/fp_layer_2. Existing train/test splits, IoU threshold, distance bins, sampled point counts and epoch budgets are retained. Newly disclosed implementation settings do not establish that existing experiments were rerun differently.

E4.justification: V1 tests rule-based uncertainty, auxiliary width and regularization strength. V2 retains these and adds direct granularity comparisons (Table 2b), auxiliary-loss-weight and attachment-layer sensitivity studies (Appendix A.5), and additional qualitative cases (Figure 5). These substantially expand validation of the central design choices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Self-training rounds and predicted box uncertainty are not statistical uncertainty estimates for the reported performance.

E6.justification: The reported T=10 Lyft APBEV/AP3D changes from 59.8/56.1 to 61.4/57.1 over 0–80m. The 50–80m entry changes from 28.5/24.9 to 36.8/29.0, while 0–30m falls from 76.0/73.4 to 74.1/71.2 (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 1b). The cause is unspecified. NuScenes main results and existing ablation scores remain unchanged, while substantial new ablation and qualitative results are added.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3 express the same absolute prediction discrepancy, exponential uncertainty weighting and weighted branch-loss combination using more explicit coordinate notation. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The central uncertainty-estimation and regularization contributions remain. The abstract's claimed Lyft APBEV/AP3D advantage increases from 2.2/1.0 to 4.1/2.0 percentage points; v1 Table 2 actually supports 2.5/1.0. The headline nuScenes advantage of 6.9/2.5 remains unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations linking equal branch-loss weights to balanced learning and earlier attachment to greater auxiliary-branch independence (Appendix A.5), alongside explanations of the granularity results. Appendix A.1 explicitly states that object categories are not modeled. The existing noise/disagreement explanation is largely retained.

D1.justification: V2 adds layer-by-layer architecture specifications, augmentation ranges, point-shuffling instructions, optimizer-policy and learning-rate-clipping details, per-GPU batching, four A6000 GPUs, and training-time estimates (Section 4.1; Appendix A.1–A.2). The code pointer changes from UL3D to UA3D. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing corresponding implementation changes.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including UNION, ProposalContrast, reward finetuning and recent uncertainty work. The uncertainty-regression discussion replaces He et al. (2020) with the distinct He et al. (2019) paper. The overall related-work taxonomy and positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanations and experimental narrative undergo extensive rewriting. UL3D becomes UA3D, contribution bullets are consolidated, rule-based baseline definitions move into the ablation discussion, and a structured appendix is added. The editorial changes extend well beyond inserting new results.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redesigned, and Figures 3–4 gain stronger contrast, revised annotations and reordered panels. Separate benchmark and ablation tables are consolidated into multipart tables. V2 adds architecture and sensitivity tables, further qualitative comparisons and an uncertainty-visualization diagram (Figures 5–6).

improvement.justification: V2 adds a direct test of the central coordinate-level design (Table 2b), supporting sensitivity studies (Appendix A.5), and substantially fuller reproduction details (A.1–A.2). These address important validation and documentation gaps in v1, while redesigned diagrams clarify the method. Unexplained Lyft score revisions and absent repeated-run uncertainty remain limitations, but the substantial quality gain rests on stronger evidence and transparency rather than higher scores alone.
